review.summary: approve_with_nits. Ran the PR's checks: 23 tests pass, link checker bad 0. The shared harness itself could not be fetched (no network), so its inputs are unverified. Top findings: (1) REVIEW.md now says linked pages are not in the material while config keeps include_dependents: true and the extra-checks list still asks to review linked pages; (2) nine decision-log rows still point at BACKLOG items this PR deletes, with no superseding rows; (3) the weekly review now rests on the Saturday task's PR firing pull_request: opened, which was not shown.

findings.checklist_item: REVIEW.md: Scopes table and 'Extra checks for pr scope'
findings.title: REVIEW.md contradicts itself and the config on whether linked pages are in the material
findings.claim: Line 92 tells the reviewer that pages linking to a changed page are not in the material and must be searched for, but line 107 still asks it to review 'pages that link to the changed ones', and review/config.yaml line 113 keeps `include_dependents: true`. One of the three is wrong, and the reviewer cannot tell which from its instructions.
findings.evidence: REVIEW.md:92 'Pages that link to a changed page are not in the material: search for its file name.' REVIEW.md:107 'Review the diff in context, including pages that link to the changed ones'. review/config.yaml:113 'include_dependents: true'. In this very run the material did include weeks/week-07-evaluation-2-and-iteration.md, a page that links to the changed README.md, so the old harness honoured the key; whether the shared harness does could not be checked (network blocked).
findings.proposed_change: Decide which is true for the shared harness. If it honours include_dependents, restore 'pages that link to them' to the pr-scope Input cell and drop the new sentence on line 92. If it does not, remove `include_dependents` from config.yaml and reword line 107 to 'search for pages that link to the changed ones'. Test: run one review and check the material list in the archived record.

findings.checklist_item: reviews/decisions.md header: never edit a decided row, add a new one that supersedes it
findings.title: Nine decision rows still point at BACKLOG items this PR deletes; nothing in the log closes them
findings.claim: The 'Fixed in' cells of PR8-3-F4, PR8-3-F3, PR8-2-F4, PR8-2-F3, PR8-2-F2, PR8-F4, PR8-F3, PR8-F2 and PR6-F7 name BACKLOG.md items that the diff removes. The log's own rule is that a decision changes only through a superseding row, and the PR description's reasons (seven fixed in cross-model-review#6, one by design, one done here) are recorded only in the PR text and a CHANGELOG line, which a reader of the log never sees.
findings.evidence: BACKLOG.md diff removes the eight 2026-10-22 harness items and the PR6-F7 item; reviews/decisions.md lines 30, 31, 35, 36, 37, 41, 42, 43 and 47 still read 'BACKLOG.md: 2026-10-22 item ...' or 'BACKLOG.md item "Rule 6 ..."'. CHANGELOG.md:14 says 'Backlog items about the old harness dropped (fixed upstream, or no longer apply)'.
findings.proposed_change: Add nine superseding rows at the top of the table (for example PR8-2-F2 superseded: decision 'accept', reason 'fixed by the shared harness design: the PR is tested as pushed', Fixed in 'cross-model-review#6' or 'this PR (#<n>)'), or, if that is too heavy, keep a short 'Closed' section at the bottom of BACKLOG.md listing each dropped item, its decision ID and where it was fixed. Either way a reader following a decision row should land on an explanation.

findings.checklist_item: README 'How it's reviewed' and REVIEW.md Roles: say who reviews what
findings.title: 'GPT reviews every PR' has two exceptions the text does not state
findings.claim: README line 52 and REVIEW.md line 19 say GPT (through Codex) reviews each PR. The config routes codex/ branches to Opus (default_reviewer: opus), and the PR text says fix PRs opened by /respond are not reviewed automatically. README's 'Answering' bullet does not mention that the fix PR gets no automatic review, so a reader may wait for one.
findings.evidence: README.md:52 'GPT (through Codex) reviews each pull request when it opens'; REVIEW.md:19 'GPT (through Codex) on PRs'; review/config.yaml:34 'default_reviewer: opus' for the codex author; config.yaml:94-96 'Fix PRs opened by /respond are not'.
findings.proposed_change: README line 52: 'GPT (through Codex) reviews each pull request written by Claude when it opens (fix PRs opened by /respond are not reviewed automatically; comment /review on them if wanted).' REVIEW.md line 19: 'GPT (through Codex) on PRs written by Claude; Opus on PRs from codex/ branches; Fable for the monthly project review or on request'.

findings.checklist_item: STYLE.md 'Contents list' and 'Visuals': commands are given as python3
findings.title: RESPOND.md says `python tools/...` where STYLE.md says `python3`; make_toc rule sits under 'Diagrams'
findings.claim: The diff changes rules 5 and 6 from python3 to python while STYLE.md still uses python3 for render_diagrams.py and make_toc.py. Small, but the author model follows these files literally. The new make_toc sentence (the PR6-F7 fix) is appended to the diagrams rule rather than being its own rule or sitting with the test rule.
findings.evidence: review/RESPOND.md:31-34 (PR version) vs STYLE.md 'run `python3 tools/make_toc.py`' and 'Render with `python3 tools/render_diagrams.py <name>`'.
findings.proposed_change: Use python3 in both files (or python in both), and move 'After adding or renaming a heading in a week file, run tools/make_toc.py' into rule 4 (headings) or a rule of its own.

findings.title: Contract tests are deleted with no replacement; REVIEW.md and schema.json can now drift apart silently
findings.claim: The removed test_review_contract.py checked that every verdict, severity and verified_by value in review/schema.json is defined in REVIEW.md, that config paths exist, and that the decision log keeps its nine columns. REVIEW.md and review/schema.json stay in this repo, so these checks still apply, and they need only json and pathlib (pyyaml was dropped from requirements.txt).
findings.evidence: Diff deletes tests/test_review_contract.py (test_every_schema_enum_is_documented_in_review_md, test_config_points_at_existing_files, test_decision_log_has_expected_columns); requirements.txt now lists pytest only.
findings.proposed_change: Keep a small tests/test_review_contract.py with the enum-documented and decision-log-columns checks (json only). If the shared harness validates config paths at load, say so in config.yaml's header and drop that check.

findings.title: Shared workflows are pinned to @main with secrets: inherit
findings.claim: Both callers use joshxinjie/cross-model-review/...@main and inherit every repo secret, including CODEX_AUTH_JSON and SECRETS_WRITE_TOKEN (which can rewrite this repo's secrets). Any change on the shared repo's main takes effect here at once, with no review in this repo. Both repos belong to the owner, so this is a fragility note, not a security finding.
findings.evidence: review.yml:45 'uses: joshxinjie/cross-model-review/.github/workflows/review.yml@main', :50 'secrets: inherit'; respond.yml same pattern. PR text: SECRETS_WRITE_TOKEN has 'Secrets: Read and write'.
findings.proposed_change: Pin to a tag or commit SHA in both `uses:` lines and set harness-ref to the same value; bump both together when the shared harness changes. Add a one-line note in config.yaml's header on how to bump.

findings.title: Does the Saturday task's PR fire pull_request: opened? The weekly review now depends on it
findings.claim: The Saturday cron that reviewed the open weekly/ PR is removed; the weekly review now happens only if the update task's PR triggers the `opened` event. GitHub does not start workflows for PRs created with GITHUB_TOKEN. The weekly commits are authored 'Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>' (a scheduled Claude Code task), which likely opens the PR through the Claude GitHub App or a token that does fire events, but the PR text only verified that an opened PR routes to gpt, not that the task's PR produces the event.
findings.evidence: review.yml:12 'types: [labeled, opened, reopened, ready_for_review]'; the diff removes 'cron: "23 3 * * 6"'. git log: 08bcc8c 'Weekly update 2026-10-24' by Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>. PR text: 'A PR that opens goes to gpt' (a config check). GitHub docs on GITHUB_TOKEN not triggering workflows: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow
findings.proposed_change: Confirm on the first Saturday after merge that a review is posted on the weekly PR without a /review comment. If it is not, either add the `review` label from the update task or restore the Saturday cron as a `schedules` entry if the shared harness supports a pr-scope schedule. Note the fallback in README 'How it's reviewed' until confirmed.

findings.title: cli_version comment refers to a 'codex-version' input that neither caller workflow passes
findings.claim: The gpt reviewer pins `cli_version: 0.164.0` with the comment 'keep in step with the workflows' codex-version input', but review.yml and respond.yml pass only harness-ref, install, check and label. Either the shared workflows have a codex-version default that must match this pin (then the comment should say where that default lives), or the comment is stale and one of the two values is unused.
findings.evidence: review/config.yaml:67; .github/workflows/review.yml `with:` block (harness-ref, install, label); .github/workflows/respond.yml `with:` block (harness-ref, install, check). The shared repo could not be fetched in this session to check its inputs.
findings.proposed_change: Either pass `codex-version: 0.164.0` explicitly in both caller workflows next to harness-ref, or reword the comment to name the file in cross-model-review that holds the default and say that the two must agree. Test: run `/review` once and check the Codex CLI version printed in the run log matches the pin.
